judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: Spillover (Q1) and whether the counter-narrative mitigates it (Q2); representation is only in the quote.

central_claim.note: Ad's harm and the counter-narrative's near-complete offset ('almost entirely ameliorated'); omits that the ad improved feelings of representation. Two of the three quotes are marked NOT IN PAPER (curly vs straight quotes); the p.1 'vastly ameliorated' quote is in the paper, so the entry is grounded.

evidence.note: Survey experiment on Prolific with 2,439 self-identified Democrats in three arms (counts in the quote); outcomes appear only in a quote.

key_findings.note: Keeps 'before the Trump ad' and 'relative to the ad alone'. Quote cited as p.10; it is on p.11.

flags.text: 'A finding that ran counter to the pre-registered hypothesis' is attached to both outcomes. Feelings of representation were 'not hypothesized' (p.11); only the motives estimate runs against H2B's stated direction, and the paper itself calls H2B supported (the F-n1 tension).

key_findings.note: Same substance as F3; treated like the parallel entry in run2.

flags.text: Says system-impacted respondents were more positive 'across all items and treatment arms'; the paper says so 'with only one exception' (p.16), which the quote keeps but the claim drops.

key_findings.note: Main effect of system-impacted status is accurate but not gold; the larger ad effect for system-impacted respondents is part of F6 (the counter-narrative heterogeneity is not stated). The ad part keeps the paper's 'appearing more damaging' (p.14).

scope_and_limits.note: Durability (and other contexts / less transparent designs). Mentions 'conducted after the election' only as context, without the campaign-period consequence, so no L6 credit.
First quote is unrelated (replication), second supports the claim.

flags.text: 'Disputes this': the paper qualifies the emotional-mobilization evidence ('this is not necessarily concrete', p.3) rather than disputing it.

interlocutor_claim.note: Attribution of refs 30-32 (Abramowitz & Webster; Kushner Gadarian & Brader; Versteegen) is correct. Policy alignment mattering for feelings of representation, set against affect, is I5 (as the calibration judge credited a similar entry). The emotional-support claim the paper qualifies is the body of work behind I4, not the one anger-ads study, so partial I4.
